implementation_notes: The default Rust realization bakes the type catalogue into the binary as const TypeSpec values, indexes them once into a static registry, and gives every entity a shared reference (&'static TypeSpec, or &'a TypeSpec tied to the registry) plus its own state. Behaviour that varies per type is a plain fn pointer in the descriptor (or a Box<dyn Behaviour> when it needs state); the std LazyLock (1.80) is what makes the static registry ergonomic, with OnceLock (1.70) as the older building block. Rust has no classes and no user-defined runtime type objects, so the descriptor, its slots and the registry are all hand-written - but the pattern needs exactly this much machinery. When the set of types is closed, an enum plus match is the idiomatic, compile-checked alternative.
pitfalls: &'static descriptors cannot come from files read at runtime: either keep the catalogue in code, or leak/replace it - runtime-loaded types need the Arc variant below.
A descriptor borrowed from a lock guard (RwLockReadGuard) ties the entity's lifetime to the guard; clone an Arc (or copy the needed values) instead of holding the reference.

fn pointers cannot capture state, so a behaviour that needs configuration must be a trait object (Box<dyn Trait>) or a parameter passed at call time; and a LazyLock initializer that panics poisons the registry for the whole process.

variants.name: Arc<TypeSpec> registry built from data at startup
variants.idiom_name: Arc<TypeSpec> + RwLock<HashMap<String, Arc<TypeSpec>>> loaded from files
variants.implementation_notes: When the type catalogue is data (JSON/TOML shipped with the game or edited by designers), the descriptors are deserialised at startup and stored as Arc<TypeSpec> in a RwLock<HashMap<..>> registry; entities clone the Arc, so the descriptor outlives them regardless of registry reloads, and types can be replaced or added without rebuilding - the pattern's actual promise. Deserialisation turns functions into ids: behaviour slots store an enum tag or &'static fn resolved from the tag, since serde cannot build closures. Choose this variant whenever types must be editable after the build; choose the static variant when the catalogue is compiled in.
pitfalls: Holding the read guard while cloning leads to deadlocks or long lock hold times; clone the Arc and drop the guard immediately.
Descriptors loaded from files are untrusted input: a missing field, a duplicate id or an out-of-range value must be rejected at load time, because the compiler cannot check any of it.
Reloading the registry replaces descriptors without touching existing entities, so half the population can run on the old type data; version descriptors and migrate deliberately.
